_partNote: Almost every stage of a biologics process is a vessel of some kind, so the seven tiles are separated by form factor rather than by function: a flat disc (culture dish), an upright tank with a top-mounted drive, a squat horizontal slab stack (filter cassettes), a tall thin flanged column, a small capped vial, a closed twisted loop (plasmid), and a limp flat bag. No two share a silhouette, and each subject is a static object that could sit still on a bench.

partPrompts.1: A shallow round culture dish lying flat on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a low straight-sided disc many times wider than it is tall, its open face scattered with a few dozen small round colonies of varying size, and its flat round lid leaning upright against one side of the dish. Flat and disc-shaped, no tank, no flask, no vessel and no equipment.
partPrompts.2: A stirred-tank bioreactor standing on three splayed legs, seen three-quarter: an upright cylinder about twice as tall as it is wide with a domed head at the top and a dished bottom, and a squat drive motor block seated dead center on the top head with a short stub shaft below it. Two small round sight ports on the shoulder and three plain pipe stubs on the side. The top-mounted motor and the legs are what identify it. One closed vessel, not a cutaway, nothing shown inside, no pipe runs leading off to other equipment.
partPrompts.3: A stack of five flat rectangular filter cassettes clamped between two thicker end plates, seen three-quarter: identical thin slabs pressed face to face into a squat block that is clearly wider and deeper than it is tall, the layered edges visible as stripes along the side, with three short round port stubs on the exposed front edge. Flat, low and horizontal; no cylinder, no tank, no vessel of any kind.
partPrompts.4: A slender packed chromatography column standing upright on a small round base, seen three-quarter: a straight smooth tube roughly six times taller than it is wide, closed at each end by a thicker flanged end cap with one small port at its center, the packed bed showing through the clear wall as an even fine texture filling the lower four-fifths. Tall and thin, no motor, no legs, no jacket; not a stirred tank.
partPrompts.5: One small vial standing upright and drawn large, seen three-quarter: a squat cylindrical body only about one and a half times as tall as it is wide, with a rounded shoulder narrowing to a short neck, a stopper seated in the neck and a crimped ring cap over it with a raised flip-off button on top. A flat solid cake sits in the bottom of the vial. One object only, no syringe, no tray, no machine; not a tall slim column.
partPrompts.6: A single closed loop of double-stranded DNA lying flat on a plain surface: one continuous slender twisted ribbon that crosses back over itself three or four times so it reads as a supercoiled ring rather than a plain circle, with no loose ends anywhere because the loop is closed. One bold looping object drawn as line work; not a straight ladder, not a short length of helix, no vessel, no equipment, nothing floating around it.
partPrompts.7: A flat single-use bag lying on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a limp rectangular pillow of thin film with softly rounded corners, bulging gently in the middle where it holds liquid and creased at the edges, with a reinforced strip along the top edge carrying two small hanging holes and two short flexible tubes leaving one corner. Soft, flat and floppy; nothing rigid, nothing cylindrical, no frame and no machine.
